passage: Tuesday, 9:40 pm. Ugh. Sat on my bed for an hour just staring at the wall. In the canteen today a boy from 9B asked me, "So is it true you still sleep with the light on?" I told exactly one person that. Vidya. Nobody else. My ears went hot and my stomach dropped like on a swing, and I laughed like it was nothing. Later, in the corridor, I asked Vidya quietly whether she had told anyone. She looked at her shoes and said, "It just came out." I said I was hurt and walked off before I said anything worse. Mum asked why I wasn't eating and I said headache. Tomorrow I'll tell Vidya calmly that I trusted her, and that I'll think before telling her things now. It's not my fault I trusted her. If it still feels this bad, I'll tell Mum. — Pranav

qa.q: What did the boy from 9B ask Pranav in the canteen?
qa.a: He asked whether it was true Pranav still sleeps with the light on.

qa.q: What is Pranav feeling after the canteen, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Sick and exposed. Pranav's ears went hot, the stomach dropped, and Pranav skipped eating, telling Mum it was a headache.

qa.q: What is Pranav's plan, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: Pranav will speak to Vidya calmly, be careful about what to share with her from now on, and go to Mum if it keeps hurting. That protects Pranav without a blow-up.

qa.q: How might Vidya have felt in the corridor?
qa.a: Probably ashamed or uneasy. Looking at her shoes and saying "It just came out" suggests she knows she slipped, though we cannot be certain.

grounding: Pranav's private confidence has spread, leaving Pranav hurt and exposed, and Pranav plans a calm confrontation and adult support.

passage:
Monday. Behind the school water tank, Joseph told Jasleen what he hadn't told anyone. His father had lost his job, and they might have to move to Kottayam. "Please don't tell."
Wednesday. In the canteen, a boy from the next section said, "Hey, Joseph, heard your dad's jobless. Selling your bike?" Two others laughed. Joseph felt sick. Only one person knew. He looked across at Jasleen, who suddenly found her lunch very interesting.
He didn't shout. After class he said, quietly, "I trusted you. You told." She mumbled that she'd only told one friend.
Friday. Joseph couldn't eat, couldn't focus. He went to his class teacher, Mrs Rego, after the bell. She listened to all of it, then said, "Telling a friend was not a mistake. The mistake was theirs." She spoke to the boys that afternoon and phoned Joseph's mother before he reached home.
He'd still say hello to Jasleen. He just wouldn't tell her anything big again.

qa.q: Where did Joseph tell Jasleen his secret?
How did Joseph feel when the boy mentioned his father in the canteen?
qa.a: He felt sick and exposed, realising only Jasleen could have spread his private news.

qa.q: Which steps helped Joseph, and why?
qa.a: He confronted Jasleen calmly, rethought what to share with her, and told Mrs Rego, who acted that same afternoon.

qa.q: How might Jasleen feel when Joseph confronts her?
qa.a: She seems ashamed and defensive, avoiding his eyes and mumbling that she only told one friend.

grounding: A teen whose best friend spreads his private news confronts her calmly, reassesses the friendship, and tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Parul, sit. You've been crying since your friend's message. Let me tell you something.
When I was sixteen, in Nagpur, my best friend was Ravi. I told him I was terrified of the board exams, that I cried the night before every test. The next week the whole class was calling me "Rona-dhona Chaitanya." I felt sick. I wanted the ground to open.
For days I thought it was my fault for trusting him. My grandmother told me, "Trusting is not a sin, beta. Breaking trust is."
So I went to Ravi. Didn't shout. I said, "You told everyone. That hurt." He went red and said sorry.
Here's the turning point. I didn't cut him off, but I stopped telling him my deepest things. We played cricket, we joked. My fears I took to my grandmother instead. Ravi and I are still friends. Just a different kind.

qa.q: What nickname did the class give young Chaitanya?
How did young Chaitanya feel when the class started teasing him?
qa.a: He felt sick and exposed, and for days he blamed himself for trusting Ravi.

qa.q: What choice did Chaitanya make after the apology, and why did it help?
qa.a: He stayed friends with Ravi but shared deep fears with his grandmother instead, which protected him while keeping the friendship.

qa.q: How might Ravi have felt when young Chaitanya confronted him calmly?
qa.a: Ravi likely felt ashamed and caught out, going red and apologising because Chaitanya did not shout.

grounding: An elder recalls being hurt when a best friend spread his secret, confronting him calmly, and changing what he shared.
